subject: Budget range validation & procurement thresholds - post-call recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@paybridge.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-20T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap - token volumes & budget bands

Hi Alex / Kelly - thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a few asks so we can validate pricing and procurement next steps.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Expected pilot volume: ~5-20M tokens/month (generation-heavy; ~80% generation, 20% embeddings).
- Target production (post-pilot): 30-50M tokens/month over next 6-12 months depending on feature rollout.
- Primary success metric: cost per 1M tokens target and predictable monthly spend for procurement.

Pricing ask from your side:
- Can you confirm your target $/1M tokens (range) that would make this commercially viable? You mentioned a target monthly spend band of roughly $4k-10k during pilot.
- Procurement thresholds: what is the threshold that triggers PO / legal review vs. CC-enabled purchases?

What we (Redwood) will provide this week:
- A rough unit economics sheet (attached) with model-level $/1M token estimates for hosted vs. dedicated capacity.
- A mutual action plan draft to map procurement milestones and timelines.

Next steps / asks:
1) Alex - confirm the monthly spend band you're comfortable with for the pilot and the procurement threshold for POs (> $X).
2) I'll loop in Neha to provide a quick unit-economics sketch and pricing levers (discount tiers for commit).
3) If that aligns, propose a procurement sync next week to walk PO/approval steps.

Attachments: pricing_model_v1.xlsx (pricing worksheet)

Thanks - Marissa

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@paybridge.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap - token volumes & budget bands

Marissa - thanks for the summary. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Pilot budget band: the team is comfortable with $4k-10k/month on a credit card (no PO) for proof-of-value. Anything expected to regularly exceed ~$10k/month will require a PO and finance review.
2) Procurement thresholds: purchases over $25k require a formal PO and SOW; anything over $50k needs legal sign-off and usually goes through a 3-4 week procurement cycle.
3) $/1M tokens: we don't have a hard internal target, but we're looking for competitive unit economics. For reference, we'd be evaluating generation pricing and embeddings separately - embeddings are used heavily for search and will be material.

Can you and Neha call out: a) your hosted $/1M tokens for generation and embeddings, b) discount tiers at different commit levels (monthly and annual), and c) whether caching/prefix optimizations could materially lower our spend given our usage profile.

Happy to jump on a 30-min procurement sync next Tue (3/24) if that works.

Alex
Alex Johnson | Head of Platform Integrations, PayBridge
alex.johnson@paybridge.com | +1 212-555-0147

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@paybridge.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-23T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap - unit economics + procurement options

Hi Alex - appreciate the detail. Quick, pragmatic numbers below to help you evaluate. These are ballpark hosted prices (single-tenant/dedicated will change economics):

Hosted (estimate, per 1M tokens):
- Generation (standard open LLM family): $2,500 / 1M tokens
- Embeddings (medium size): $550 / 1M tokens

Committed tiers / discounts (examples):
- 10% off at 10-20M tokens/month commit (12-month term)
- 15% off at 30-50M tokens/month commit (12-month term)
- Dedicated capacity pricing available for sustained >50M tokens/month (fixed monthly) - we can model that if you expect growth.

Optimization levers that change $/1M effective cost:
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (can reduce generation tokens by ~10-35% depending on reuse).
- Batching and request shaping - reduces NPU cost and can lower per-token price at high throughput.
- Quantization/model selection - using a cheaper variant for non-critical flows reduces unit cost.

Given your stated pilot band ($4k-10k/month):
- At $2,500 / 1M gen, $4k buys ~1.6M generation tokens (plus embeddings separately).
- If your pilot is 5-20M tokens/month total, hosted costs at list could be $12.5k-50k/month (generation-dominant). So your pilot band suggests either: a) you plan to only enable a small subset of features initially (1-5M tokens), or b) we need to apply a committed discount/pooled pricing or optimize usage to hit $4k-10k.

Procurement options to match thresholds:
- Pilot on CC: we can scope a CC-enabled PoV up to $10k/month (no PO).
- Short-term committed pilot: 3-6 month commit with a capped monthly spend and a mid-tier discount to keep monthly invoiced amounts within $10k-25k.
- Full enterprise: >$25k/month goes via PO + standard SOW and we can include custom SLAs and audit clauses.

Next steps (suggested):
1) Marissa / Alex: confirm the pilot scope (expected active users / endpoints) so we can map to token volumes.
2) I'll prepare a short options table (hosted list, hosted with 12mo commit discounts, and dedicated baseline) and circulate by end of day tomorrow. (pricing_model_v1.xlsx updated attached)
3) If you want procurement aligned for Tue 3/24, we can run through the options and pick one that fits your PO thresholds.

- Neha
